chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: The TOBA theatres and playing spot dates
summary: He says they played negro theatres in Indianapolis, Louisville and Philadelphia on spot dates, not a TOBA contract.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I'm sure that Buck and Bubbles also did perform in TOBA --

You began -- you began that. This whole sequence of TOBA, the whole thing you began with. That was TOBA you started with. That was a negro theater in Indianapolis. There was a negro theater in Louisville. There was a negro theater in Nashville that I told you about. The Sander

Theater in Philadelphia was a negro theater. That's the TOBA circuit. But who had a contract for the circuit. I didn't have no contract. We didn't have no contract for the circuit. We only played spot. We played spot. We'd be playing in Philadelphia this month and next month we'd be playing in Chicago at the Regal Theater. See? That's the way that goes.
So now what's the other question? Give me another.
